Writing density functions

The multifit utility lets you fit multiple instances of a model to a dataset, with control over shared and independent parameters. The model itself depends on the process being described and as such is left to the user.

Because multifit is intended to fit binned data, the model must take the form of a cumulative density function (CDF). The `numba-stats`_ package implements jit-compiled CDFs for a number of common distributions, and is a good place to start.

Note:

multifit plans to provide CDFs for some additional distributions, such as polynomials between limits.

Use different models in the same dataset

If the data contains structures with different functional forms, but which nevertheless gain from simultaneous fitting, one can introduce a switching parameter selecting which function will be calculated, as for example

def cdf_with_switching(x, c, p1, p2, p3):
    if c == 1:
        return cdf_1(x, p1, p2)
    else:
        return cdf_2(x, p1, p3)

Here, the switching parameter c determines which functional form is used. This parameter can the be fixed in the input file for each instance of a peak structure.
